label: early original-phase inputs of r/o/s/t/3/x/p/z/f
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.9% of mass). It never fires on the delimiter and essentially never in the copy phase. It is token-selective: the input token is one of r, o (strongest, rate about 0.3), s, t, 3, x, p, z or f; i, l and 2 rarely fire. It is also position-selective: activity peaks at t=1..3 (about 80% of mass) and decays at later positions and at longer L. The largest activations are r or o at t=2..3 after neutral letters (e.g. 0 k r r, y h r r). About 93% of mass falls on the first occurrence of the token. Whether a given token at a given position fires depends on the preceding context in ways no simple predicate captured (e.g. h o does not fire), so precision is only about 0.5. The broader predicate with t<=4 reaches 0.92 mass recall but 0.40 precision.
